title.zh: 体积归一化指数源剖面

summary: Discrete volume-normalized exponential source profile on a nonuniform normalized-radius cell grid

identity.relation: Discrete exponential source with signed float64-tiny width floor and supplied-volume normalization
identity.definition: For finite nonzero width set w_safe=copysign(max(abs(width),float64 tiny),width). Let ref be the final rho for positive width and first rho for negative width. Set S_i=exp((rho_i-ref)/w_safe), and return total*S_i/sum_j(S_j*vpr_j*drho_norm_j). decay_start cancels identically. The tiny-width floor retains the repaired source numerical convention.
identity.model: Discrete normalized radial source shape with float64 output and extended intermediate arithmetic
identity.geometry: Normalized radial cell grid with explicit volume metric and quadrature weights
identity.boundary: Discrete cell-volume sum; no extrapolation or hidden endpoint reconstruction
assumptions: All grid vectors are equal-length, finite and one-dimensional.
Positive width increases with rho; negative width decreases with rho.

inputs.name: rho_norm
inputs.dtype: Python/NumPy real integer or floating array converted to float64; boolean, complex, string and masked inputs rejected

inputs.name: drho_norm
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; same shape as rho_norm.

inputs.name: decay_start
inputs.description: Reference decay location; cancels under normalization.

inputs.name: width
inputs.constraints: Finite nonzero real scalar for finite result; zero/nonfinite return NaNs.

outputs.name: profile
outputs.constraints: Finite on successful return for finite nonzero widths; zero/nonfinite width returns all NaN.

preconditions: All grid vectors are equal-length, finite and one-dimensional.
Positive width increases with rho; negative width decreases with rho.
supported: Nonuniform grids, conservation, signed/integer/tiny widths, decay-start cancellation and malformed inputs.
excluded: Decay_start has no effect on normalized values by the source relation.
No continuous quadrature claim beyond supplied cell weights.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for malformed types/shapes, nonfinite grid, decay_start or total, or nonpositive weights. After those checks, a width of zero, NaN or either infinity returns an all-NaN profile.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError for overflowed finite output or when rounding the float64 profile loses the requested discrete integral beyond 64 float64 epsilons relative, with zero absolute tolerance. Negligible tails may underflow to zero.

provenance.lineage_summary: Derived from TORAX mathematical source-profile and stored-energy relations. The numerical formulation retains the repaired integer-width and tiny-width source behavior and explicit cell-volume integration; SciRel independently validates the declared arrays and scalar shapes.
source_kinds: SciRel numerical implementation and independent validation
provenance.license_status: TORAX-derived relations retain Apache-2.0 attribution and the full source license in the selected distribution.

python.signature: exponential_profile(rho_norm, vpr, drho_norm, *, decay_start, width, total)

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.source import exponential_profile
r=np.array([.2,.6]); v=np.array([2.,3.]); d=np.array([.4,.6])
p=exponential_profile(r,v,d,decay_start=.8,width=.2,total=4.)
assert np.isclose(np.sum(p*v*d),4.)

scope: Nonuniform grids, conservation, signed/integer/tiny widths, decay-start cancellation and malformed inputs.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent numerical probes establish the named mathematical relation, discrete conservation, boundary and shape/failure behavior. They do not establish general plasma calibration or complete edge-model validity.
known_limitations: Decay_start has no effect on normalized values by the source relation.
No continuous quadrature claim beyond supplied cell weights.
Extended-intermediate checks were executed on Linux x86_64 with NumPy longdouble; platforms whose longdouble has no extended range are not computationally qualified for extreme-scale cases.
No array-parameter broadcasting or batch axis: all grid inputs are equal-length vectors and profile parameters are scalar-shaped.
